lens.message:
Here's the shift: saving a memory enrolls its creator as a reviewer — held from here on as a binding rule of the verification workflow, not a side effect of storage. The act of saving and the act of assigning review rights are now the same act.

What it changes our approach to: who appears on a memory's reviewers list · what saving a memory does in the workflow · what the e2e suite asserts about reviewer enrollment.

The line carrying it, from Xena ExpertGH: "Decision: the e2e suite asserts that saving a memory enrolls its creator as a reviewer."

Before/after, on the probe itself (.aswritten/memories/2026-09-23-1-review-enrollment-probe.md, "Review enrollment probe"):

As written: "Decision: the e2e suite asserts that saving a memory enrolls its creator as a reviewer. This probe memory exists only to carry that assertion."

Through the shift: this reads as the rule performing itself, not a report about a test — saving this very memory put its creator on the reviewers list (the frontmatter already carries xena+staging@aswritten.ai), and the e2e suite treats that enrollment as the expected outcome of every save. The probe doesn't just state the rule; it enacts it.

Right shift?

Who else it moves: honestly, no one yet — no other documents are in view on this stream, so the probe is the only place this rule currently lives. One narrower shift is parked for its own pass: probe memories as deliberate fixtures, the memory store doubling as the test suite.

Nothing to apply across yet — want me to hold this as the shift for the stream, so the next documents touching reviewers or the memory lifecycle get read through it?
